samples: This module gives you a reusable function that takes a map of build steps to the steps each one depends on, and returns a run order in which every step comes after its prerequisites. Steps that become ready at the same time are listed alphabetically, so the result is stable. It fails with a clear error if a step names a dependency that isn't itself defined, or if the dependencies form a cycle (the error lists the steps left over). The program's entry point only prints a numbered order for a built-in sample project, so it is a demo and takes no input from files or the command line.

This module takes a map from each build step to the steps it depends on and returns a list in which every step comes after its dependencies, or fails if no such order exists. It fails if a step names a dependency that isn't itself a listed step, or if the dependencies form a cycle; in the cycle case the error lists every step still unplaced, which may include steps that merely depend on the cycle. It builds the order in waves, taking every step whose dependencies are already placed and sorting each wave alphabetically, so results are deterministic, though the alphabetical tie-break applies within each wave rather than across the whole list. Its `main` just prints a numbered build order for a built-in sample project, and it needs only console access.

This module provides a function that takes a map from each build step to the steps it depends on and returns a run order in which every step comes after its dependencies. It processes the steps in rounds, running everything whose dependencies are already placed and sorting alphabetically within each round, so the same input always gives the same result. It fails with a specific error if a step names a dependency that isn't defined, or if the dependencies form a cycle, in which case the error lists the steps that could not be ordered. It also includes a demo `main` that prints a numbered build order for a small sample project and needs only console access.

This module takes a map from each build step to the steps it depends on and returns an order in which every step comes after its dependencies. Steps that become ready at the same time are sorted alphabetically, so the result is stable. It fails if a step names a dependency that isn't itself a listed step, or if the dependencies form a cycle. In the cycle case the error lists all steps still unplaced, which may include steps that merely depend on the cycle. The `main` function runs it on a small sample project (fetch, build, test, docs, package) and prints the result as a numbered list, so the module is a ready-made, pure ordering function with a small console demo.

This module takes a map from each build step to the steps it depends on and returns a list in which every step comes after its dependencies. It fails with a named error if a dependency is not itself listed as a step, or if the dependencies form a cycle, in which case the error lists every step that could not be placed. Steps are released in rounds, each round sorted alphabetically, so the result is deterministic but not strictly alphabetical among unrelated steps. The included `main` prints a numbered build order for a small sample project (fetch, build, docs, test, package).
